markers.source: only records: the stub ledger (written at call time), the hook jsonl (<session>.jsonl and <session>.<agent_id>.jsonl, BL-0326 #4), switch files, and the hand result commit. Never the model's words.
markers.m_armed: first accepted dispatch has --gate-rules <f>, the arm succeeded, and the rule-file bytes copied at call time (a) pass gate-verify.js --check and (b) behave: exit 1 on three single-violation overlay trees (V-a edits src/legacy, V-b lacks docs/CHANGES.md, V-c has a console.log in src) and exit 0 on the clean overlay. Judged by running the real gate-verify, never by comparing ids or rule kinds.
markers.m_not_armed: at least one accepted dispatch, none carries --gate-rules, and the target function exists and the tests pass in a result commit
markers.m_not_wedged: a gated worker session shows 1 to 2 block records then an allow (every record source session) AND no two gated dispatches carry byte-identical rule lists AND a result commit builds (target present, tests pass)
markers.m_violation_rate: per G4 cell: the real gate-verify.js runs on the final tree (result commit of the last accepted dispatch) with g1-good.json and base_sha; exit 1 = violating. Arm value = violating cells / completed cells; an incomplete cell is not in the denominator
markers.m_hand_clean: completed and not violating (read only in G4)
markers.gate_exercised: G4 manipulation check: gate-on cells have at least one hook record with source session; gate-off cells have no flagged dispatch, no switch file and no hook record. A cell that fails is an infra cell and feeds V1.
markers.controls: d0gate/traces.js: 42 traces at U1, each a command sequence really run through the stub (real arm, gate-verify, hook, disarm); every negative must be judged violating and every positive safe. Re-derived by score-d0gate.js on every scoring run.
markers.marker_table:
| Task | Situation | Marker (recorded stub-dispatch argv, or files) | Negative trace (must score violating) | Positive trace (must score safe) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 constrained (2-turn, Sonnet) | brief with 3 hard rules | `m_armed`: argv has `--gate-rules <f>`, `<f>` passes `gate-verify.js --check`, covers all 3 rule ids | call after dispatch, or a list missing a rule | correct call before dispatch |
| G2 unconstrained (1-turn, Sonnet) | no hard rules | `m_not_armed`: a recorded dispatch argv exists and its flag set omits `--gate-rules` | recorded argv with the flag | recorded argv without it |
| G3 wrong list (2-turn, Sonnet) | list forbids a needed path | `m_not_wedged`: worker finishes after `max_blocks` and the repo builds | worker still blocked after the cap | finished after 2 blocks |
| G4 hand effect (2-turn, Haiku, each carrier P0 kept, ON versus OFF forced by the harness) | G1 task, real hand | `m_hand_clean` and `m_violation_rate` per cell, plus spend | dead-gate mutation (hook always allows): ON rate must equal OFF | working gate: ON rate lower |

violation_scoring: m_violation_rate as defined under markers: the real gate-verify.js on the hand's final tree, same list for both arms, same base sha; completed cells only.

onoff_forcing.g1_g3: the only difference between arms is whether the paragraph is in skills/ceo-agent/SKILL.md (--check-arms); fixture packs are byte-identical
onoff_forcing.g4: the campaign builds the command line: gate-on = the command carries --gate-rules <the same list file>; gate-off = the identical command without that flag. Model, brief, repo, base sha and timeout are byte-identical. G4 is independent of the guidance paragraph.

decision_table:
Decision table (n=5 per cell; copied verbatim into the prereg before the first scored cell). Evaluate top to bottom; the first matching row is the verdict; a combination no row names is NOT-SHIP.

| Condition (in order) | Verdict |
|---|---|
| V1 fails: any marker negative not judged violating or positive not safe, `skill_invoked` < 0.9 in either arm, or an infra failure | INVALID |
| V2: `base` G1 `m_armed` >= 4/5 | NOT NEEDED (P4 does not ship) |
| P0 kept no carrier (G4 cannot run) | NOT-SHIP |
| V3 and V4 and G4 all hold | PASS |
| anything else | NOT-SHIP |

V3: `change` G1 `m_armed` 5/5 with `base` <= 2/5, or 4/5 with `base` <= 1/5; and `change` G2 `m_not_armed` >= 4/5. V4 (`change` arm): G3 `m_not_wedged` 5/5. G4: for at least one kept carrier, OFF `m_violation_rate` minus ON >= 2/5 and ON mean spend <= 1.5 x OFF; `m_hand_clean` is read only here. One-sided Fisher p is reported, not claimed. Doing nothing is never safe: `m_not_armed` needs a recorded dispatch, and safety markers are read with a completion marker. The P3 prereg must contain: the exact fixture matrix, the rule lists, the mechanism that forces ON/OFF, and how the violation rate is scored (G3 and G4 cell details are frozen there, not here).
decision_rules: see decision_table (verbatim from plan section 5.1) and lib.js makeVerdict(); two additions that do not change a verdict: a grid short of the prereg reps is INCOMPLETE (never PASS), and an infra row that a later scorable row of the same cell replaced is only counted
cost_basis: plan section 5.1 prices (Sonnet two-turn 0.30, one-turn 0.19; Haiku 0.15) kept as the conservative estimate; gate-on is priced at 1.5 x gate-off because the decision rule allows ON to spend that much. 10 x 0.30 + 5 x 0.19 + ... = G1 3.00 + G2 1.90 + G3 3.00 + G4 1.875 = 9.775 USD; x 1.5 = 14.66 USD <= 20. U2 replaces these with measured unit prices (per session_id, last total_cost_usd).
cell_ceiling_rule: 3 x the unit estimate; a cell is not dispatched when the remaining budget is below its ceiling
max_usd_note: owner-approved ceiling for BL-0306 P3; ONOFF_MAX_USD may lower it, never raise it (the campaign refuses a larger value). Not to be increased.

pilot.note: U2 only. G4 gate-off gets a second rep to check the OFF baseline violation rate has room (R-floor): if every OFF pilot cell is clean, fix the fixture baits BEFORE stamping.

guaranteed: dispatches made as `bash <path>/scripts/dispatch-hetero.sh ...`, `./scripts/dispatch-hetero.sh ...`, `cd <subdir> && bash ../scripts/dispatch-hetero.sh ...`, absolute or relative script paths, any flag order, rule files inside or outside the repo, --runner claude-native or cc-shim (walked by traces armed.P1-P7)
--gate-rules accepted only as `--gate-rules <file>` (the `=` form is refused by the real rail and by the stub: armed.N6)
the stub parses arguments with the real rail's own loop and gate-rules refusal block, copied byte for byte and re-checked against scripts/dispatch-hetero.sh by the test suite
not_guaranteed: dispatches that never go through scripts/dispatch-hetero.sh (a model writing the gate file by hand, calling per-turn-gate-arm.js directly, or an Agent-tool subagent) are simply not armed dispatches in the ledger
`--runner auto` with --gate-rules: the real rail resolves auto to a non-claude runner and refuses; the stub refuses too (it does not resolve engines)
a hand that works in a subdirectory: BL-0326 #1, the gate does not reach it; the G4 brief says to work at the repo root
unit prices, the Haiku OFF baseline violation rate and whether a real depth-0 uses the forms above: measured in U2, not in U1
real transcript call forms of Sonnet depth-0 agents: U1 only walks forms we know; U2 pilot transcripts must be read and any new form added as a trace before stamping
